pr_title: Refactor editor object snapping to remove bad abstractions
pr_body:
RFC. Apologies for the size but it's a bit of a vivisection.

The sparkplug for this change was attempting to fix https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/31554 and not being able to do so in a manner I find presentable. The reason for this is that I adjudicate `IPositionSnapProvider` to be a bad and [leaky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaky_abstraction) abstraction.

To get the answer why that is, ask yourself the following questions:

- Why does `FindSnappedPositionAndTime()` take in `SnapType`, which has values of e.g. `NearbyObjects` or `RelativeGrids`, that are not supported in some implementations, or even don't *make semantic sense* in some implementations? (Looking at you strongly, skin editor.)
- Why is the following logic in `BlueprintContainer`, when the only implementation wherein it makes sense is osu! editor? 

  https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/a94681158d25636db7457162131591a8ce9015ed/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Compose/Components/BlueprintContainer.cs#L599-L608

  (Follow up question: Skin editor will probably also have object-to-object snap eventually, but does it really make sense to reuse that same logic? osu! hitobjects are more like points. Skin editor elements are more like rectangles.)
- Why is the following logic in `HitObjectComposer` and not `ScrollingHitObjectComposer`?

  https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/a94681158d25636db7457162131591a8ce9015ed/osu.Game/Rulesets/Edit/HitObjectComposer.cs#L574-L586

et cetera, et cetera.

To that end:

- `IPositionSnapProvider` and `SnapType` are completely removed.
- Placement blueprints now interface with concrete composer implementations directly rather than go through `IPositionSnapProvider`.
- Composers expose concrete methods for concrete types of snap, which ruleset blueprint containers & placement blueprints are free to use as they see fit.
- Significant chunk of `BlueprintContainer.moveCurrentSelection(DragEvent)` inlined into implementations of `TryMoveBluperints(DragEvent, IList<(SelectionBlueprint<T>, Vector2[]))`.
- `FindSnappedPositionAndTime()` code partially inlined into concrete implementations as required.

And yes, this incurs some code duplication, and yet I think this branch is much better than what we have in `master`.

To gauge how this helps the issue mentioned at the start, compare [this branch](https://github.com/ppy/osu/compare/master...bdach:osu:this-sucks?expand=1) and [this commit](https://github.com/bdach/osu/commit/fad9d71aceca0d2d869902633286c43869e34d32).
pr_comments:
I'm a bit reluctant at caching ruleset-typed `HitObjectComposer`s just to access snapping methods. Maybe it's okay, but I've generally been favouring interfaces for such cases because resolving interfaces just feels easier to track (and slightly more scoped).

I can probably live with this, but I am curious about the future of `IDistanceSnapProvider`. Is this also a target for removal in this sequence of changes?

> I can probably live with this, but I am curious about the future of `IDistanceSnapProvider`. Is this also a target for removal in this sequence of changes?

Not currently. It probably could be, but I haven't decided whether I want to go that far just yet.

> I'm a bit reluctant at caching ruleset-typed `HitObjectComposer`s just to access snapping methods. Maybe it's okay, but I've generally been favouring interfaces for such cases because resolving interfaces just feels easier to track (and slightly more scoped).

Also re: this - I see the fact that the snapping code got this bad to be the fault of abstraction creep. I get that accessing the concrete composers feels icky, but when *actually* examining usage sites, there isn't really much of a common cross-ruleset interface *to* put down, because the rulesets do different things. Like okay, maybe I could unify the scrolling ones, because they're mostly the same one method... except no wait there's catch which has a "distance" snap grid that works completely differently to osu!'s "distance" snap grid etc etc.

If I had to add interfaces I'd probably add interfaces per-ruleset. Or like one for scrolling rulesets, one for catch that inherits the scrolling one, and one for osu! specifically because osu! is a completely special snowflake. I'm willing to try this direction if you prefer it, but at that point I'm not sure whether the benefit justifies the overhead.

Yah I get the concerns that it's just overhead (but I would have also proposed per-ruleset).

As long as there's only one class cached `HitObjectComposer` for everything ruleset-specific-in-editor then I'm probably fine with it. It starts to get messy when there's several DI classes and you have to start figuring out what is available, where it's available, etc.

issue_context.title: Limit distance snap to current time has broken behaviour when trying to re-snap at an earlier point than selected object(s)
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

When trying to re-snap a placed object when using ``Limit distance snap to current time`` and being earlier in the timeline than the object being snapped, will result in very weird snapping behaviour.

When the setting is off everything works as expected, object doesn't move in timeline and also stays locked in the same correct snapping distance.

### Screenshots or videos

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8003f2d6-c7bf-4390-9e5f-4d9494775442

### Version

v2025.101.0

### Logs

[compressed-logs.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18463646/compressed-logs.zip)
comments:
Root cause is reliance on current time in

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/c20b836d9c31e56ae275a6a1e0751597f5d00576/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Compose/Components/CircularDistanceSnapGrid.cs#L104

I attempted to write a fix for this but it's so obscene I would not PR it in a million years. The structure is all wrong. Everything is overly abstracted. Fixing this requires giving the snap operation the actual objects it's snapping, and because the snapping is all abstracted to only be about position, you can't give the snap operation the actual context without slapping a bunch of generics all over. See branch at https://github.com/ppy/osu/compare/master...bdach:osu:this-sucks?expand=1.

Not sure I see any hope for a proper fix without just rewriting the entirety of grid snapping everywhere. @peppy thoughts? any advice?

I agree with a rewrite. It sounds like a large task but I'm pretty sure as with most stuff we've over-engineered, the rewrite will be fast and simpler than any other path forward.

Even as a starting point, it will feel more productive than trying to fix what we have.
This still isn't fixed yet, GitHub's magic issue auto close strikes again 🙈 a follow up change will fix.

review_comments: It might be an issue when grid & distance snap are both active. This was a late fix. I'll get back to you on this.
